axes.model_access: Tool-suite form: behind each tool is a dedicated capability (background removal/cleanup/relighting/upscaling/uncrop etc., listed item by item on the official site); the text-to-image tool uses SD-family models (official-site FAQ narrative). Users pick tools, not models.
axes.runtime: Web (clipdrop.co) + API (official FAQ: the API is served via Jasper API); processing happens on the vendor's cloud.
axes.local_files: Processed results download to local; no officially stated account-side work library or local data surface — whether uploaded images are retained after processing is not verified line by line in the terms text.
axes.background: Processing is instant (single-image atomic operations, no queue concept); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified); on the API side, batching runs on the caller's own concurrency — the platform offers no managed batch processing.
axes.tools: The tool surface listed on the official site: Remove Background, Cleanup, Replace Background, Uncrop, Image Upscaler, Relight (relighting — the site's signature tool), Text Remover, Universal Resizer, Text to image; the editing toolset is the main function (inclusion criterion 1 satisfied, see inventory).
axes.context: No project/memory concept — a one-image-in, one-image-out tool flow; context is managed entirely by the caller (a human or an API integrator).
axes.permissions: The free tier has per-tool daily caps (official FAQ framing); paid tiers raise the caps (D9: prices not collected); the training-use switch is not verified line by line.
axes.fit: Fits: batch single-image atomic operations (cutout/object removal/relighting/upscaling), e-commerce product-image workflows, API integration into your own product. Does not fit: creation-oriented generation (text-to-image is a side act), style consistency, project-based management.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Relight's actual effectiveness boundary on non-product images (portraits/scenes)**
- **The real experience of the free tier's per-tool caps** (behavior after exceeding them)
- **Endpoint compatibility between the Jasper-migrated API and the old Clipdrop API**
unknowns:
- The specific model tiers behind each tool (no official statement verified)
- The training-use switch (not verified line by line)
- Whether the account side keeps processing history (no official statement verified)
- Jasper's long-term investment in the Clipdrop product line (no official statement verified)
related: Former owner: Clipdrop was once under Stability, now the API runs on Jasper terms — see the Stability dossier for its open-model main line.
Both editing-oriented: Firefly embeds in the professional design suite, Clipdrop is a standalone atomic toolset.
Editing surfaces overlap (inpainting/background replacement): Recraft has editing inside a creation bench, Clipdrop is a pure toolset.
API downstream: Clipdrop's per-tool APIs often reach batch flows through Zapier-style automation platforms — the automation side is where it scales.
sources: Clipdrop · official site (tool surface and FAQ, incl. ownership-history self-account)
